task: Some people believe that artificial intelligence should be used in schools, while others think students should learn without it. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.
essay:
Artificial intelligence is increasingly available in schools, and its educational role is widely debated. Some people believe that it provides valuable support, while others fear that it replaces independent thinking. In my view, schools should allow carefully limited AI assistance while continuing to assess what students can do for themselves.

One reason to use AI is that students do not always receive feedback when they need it. A teacher responsible for a large class may have little time to discuss every draft. An AI tool can identify an unclear sentence or ask a student to explain an unsupported claim. For example, a learner who struggles with paragraph organisation could receive questions about the purpose of each paragraph. The learner would still need to decide how to revise the text.

However, access to an immediate answer can also discourage effort. If students submit generated essays, teachers may see fluent language without knowing whether the students understand the argument. AI feedback can also be inaccurate. A confident recommendation is not necessarily a correct one, so students need opportunities to challenge suggestions rather than accept them automatically.

Schools can address these risks through clear task rules. Students could write their first drafts independently, record the feedback they used, and explain one important revision aloud. Teachers should also retain some tasks that are completed without generative tools. This would make it easier to distinguish assistance from replacement.

In conclusion, neither a complete ban nor unrestricted use is the best response. AI can support writing when teachers design tasks around student responsibility. The aim should be a learner who can justify a decision, not simply a more polished final essay.
